models_evaluated: commercial AI fracture detection tool (CE-marked, unnamed)

links.outcome: Availability of vendor documentation for CE-marked AI solutions during procurement and implementation
links.effect: Limited documentation of Conformité Européenne-marked solutions was identified as a major challenge in the procurement and implementation of the AI fracture detection tool.
links.quote: Major challenges comprised limited documentation of Conformité Européenne-marked solutions, deskilling, and misaligned financial incentives.

links.outcome: Clinician deskilling concerns during AI fracture detection implementation
links.effect: Deskilling was identified as a major challenge in the qualitative evaluation; no quantitative measure was reported.
links.quote: Major challenges comprised limited documentation of Conformité Européenne-marked solutions, deskilling, and misaligned financial incentives.

unlisted_practices: Using the NASSS framework for formative process evaluation with real-time feedback to implementation teams
Attending to clinician trust, task distribution, and digital maturity when implementing AI
Aligning financial incentives with AI implementation

screen.reason: The study conducts a real-world formative process evaluation of implementing a commercial AI fracture detection tool in Norwegian healthcare, evaluating implementation factors using the NASSS framework rather than testing a specific deployment practice with/without comparison.
